page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor with an x86_64 architecture, the instance allocates 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The CPU architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512). This instance does not include bundled local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance achieves top-tier single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2228.0 placing it in the top 10% of tested servers, alongside strong single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression rates. However, multi-core scaling is limited, with stress-ng multi-core performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falling into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is also a bottleneck; memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks, as well as the Passmark memory score, ranks in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4n-highcpu-4 offers a dense compute profile for workloads that do not require large memory allocations or high memory throughput. The inclusion of AMX and AVX-512 instructions enables efficient execution of vector and matrix operations, as demonstrated by average-tier performance in LLM prompt processing and text generation for small models. This hardware profile is suitable for single-threaded applications, text processing, static web serving, and lightweight CPU-based inference tasks.
